text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Education ministry orders school teachers to steer clear of election fray and to focus on preparing school children for upcoming exams. Teachers usually form the bulk of political parties' workers, particularly in villages.
- Officials from independent election watchdog criss-crossing country to urge local observers to step up preparations for the June 5 parliamentary elections.

- The National Democratic Rally, known by its French RND acronym, coins poll campaign motto: "Hope, Work, Solidarity". The RND, grouping President Liamine Zeroual's staunch backers, gathers its candidates in Algiers to plot campaign strategy.

- The June parliamentary elections will be test case for the authorities to foster a multi-party democracy. Hundreds of foreign observers and journalists will watch carefully the government's democratic aptitude.
- Restoring security and stability will be the main catchword in the parliamentary election campaign.

- The authorities raise to 10 out of 20 the compulsory average marks for student exam succes as about one million school children are preparing to sit exams. The previous pass mark was an average of seven out of 20. Teachers and parents fear the measure will lead to increased school dropout.

- Algeria's Societe Nationale des Vehicules Industriels (SNVI), which part-manufactures and assembles cars and commercial vehicles, signed an 800 million dinar ($14.28 million) deal to supply customised vehicles and cars to two main Algerian firms -- gas and electricity utility Sonelgaz and passenger carrier Societe Nationale du Transport Routier (SNTR). Officials and managers hailed the accord as a significant step to foster local industrial production with the help of local banks.
